movement_source: row 'Operating expenses to total operating income', column 30 Jun 25 column -> column 30 Jun 26 column
headline: CBA's headline cost-to-income ratio (Operating expenses to total operating income) fell 20bpts from 45.7% in FY25 to 45.5% in FY26. The improvement reflects positive jaws: operating income grew 6.2% (from $28,465m to $30,224m), faster than operating expenses, which grew 5.8% on a total basis (from $12,996m to $13,755m) or 5.6% on an underlying basis (from $12,866m to $13,585m). The underlying cost-to-income ratio (excluding restructuring and notable items) improved more, falling 30bpts from 45.2% to 44.9%, because restructuring and notable items rose from $130m to $170m in FY26, dampening the headline improvement.

drivers.narrative: Operating income grew 6.2% from $28,465m (FY25) to $30,224m (FY26), faster than operating expenses, producing positive jaws that lowered the cost-to-income ratio. The bank cites strong volume growth with a broadly stable underlying margin as the driver of income growth.

Operating expenses grew 5.8% (total, $12,996m to $13,755m) or 5.6% (underlying, $12,866m to $13,585m), slower than income, so jaws was positive and the ratio fell. Underlying expense growth was driven by inflation (+$455m), investment in technology (+$444m), investment in frontline and operations (+$128m) and other (+$96m), partly offset by productivity (-$404m).

Restructuring and notable items increased from $130m (FY25) to $170m (FY26), +31%, raising total operating expenses and dampening the headline ratio improvement. The underlying cost-to-income ratio (excluding these items) fell 30bpts from 45.2% to 44.9%, a larger improvement than the headline -20bpts. FY26 items relate to NZ legal settlement provisions, an ASIC Better Banking goodwill payment, and domestic customer remediation.

values: profit announcement: total operating expenses +6%, underlying +6%
disagreements.explanation: The profit announcement rounds the growth rates to whole per cent (6%), while the presentation reports more precise rates (+5.8% total, +5.6% underlying). Both derive from the same levels ($13,755m/$12,996m and $13,585m/$12,866m).

limitations: The bank does not publish a formal ppt decomposition of the cost-to-income ratio movement into income vs expense contributions; the -20bpts movement is stated as a single figure. The jaws (income growing faster than expenses) is the driver, but the ppt split between the income and expense contributions is not quantified by the bank, so contributions are left unquantified and the full -20bpts is reported as residual.

The notable-items dampening (headline -20bpts vs underlying -30bpts) is inferred from the bank's two separately-stated ratios; the bank does not explicitly attribute the 10bpts difference to notable items.

The operating expenses walk (inflation, technology, frontline/operations, other, productivity) is a walk of underlying operating expenses, not of the ratio itself; it explains the expense-growth side of jaws.
